articles.title: ‘Being Heumann’ Composer Francesco Le Metre Tapped Into Judy Heumann’s Drive And A ’70s Punk Rock Spirit – Sound & Screen Film
articles.content: For composer Francesco Le Metre , the brief when first discussing Apple Original Films ‘ disability rights drama Being Heumann with director Siân Heder was to capture the spirit of its subject, activist Judy Heumann, through music. With his score, he says, he was aiming for something “honest and intimate” — not “too big or too cinematic” — that reflected Heumann’s “personality, her drive, her humanity, but also at the same time, the impact that she had on the community.” One throughline to the score was the sense of a “call to action” — the “big punk rock,” DIY spirit of the ’70s, which Le Metre captured through drums. “We had to deconstruct the drumming a little bit, so we played very unconventional grooves, and then also the strings,” he explained in conversation at Deadline’s Sound & Screen Film. “We performed the strings with a guitar pick instead of col legno to convey the sense of punk rock and, again, the DIY spirit of the movement.” Strings also helped, Le Metre said, to capture the sense of Heumann as someone with drive and racing thoughts who was moved to act fast. “I worked on a lot of string textures, kind of like these short phrases that were bouncing one to another. And I did the same thing with the melodic writing. When it came to her humanity as well, instead of writing a straight melodic line, I had small motifs interweaving into one another, to represent her thoughts or impulse.” Being Heumann marks the Sicilian composer’s first collaboration with Heder, the director behind another inclusive disability-themed crowd-pleaser in Apple’s groundbreaking Oscar winner CODA . Ruth Madeley stars as Heumann, who in 1977, led disabled activists in an occupation of San Francisco federal offices, refusing to leave until the government implemented landmark disability-rights protections. articles.title: Kris Bowers On Creating A Love Letter To Ghana & Film History With His Score For ‘The Eyes Of Ghana’ – Sound & Screen Film
articles.content: “We wanted this score to be a love letter to Ghana and to the history of film,” Kris Bowers says of his work on The Eyes of Ghana , the latest feature from Canadian filmmaker Ben Proudfoot. The Oscar-winning musician was speaking at Deadline’s Sound & Screen Film event, where a live orchestra performed parts of Bowers’ score. Directed by Proudfoot, with Barack and Michelle Obama and content creator IShowSpeed on board as producers, The Eyes of Ghana spotlights Chris Hesse, the 93-year-old forgotten personal cinematographer of revolutionary African leader Kwame Nkrumah. The Eyes of Ghana details the rise and fall of Nkrumah, a towering figure of African history who served as Ghana’s first President and led decolonial efforts across the continent. Nkrumah was toppled in 1966 by a CIA-orchestrated military coup. As a result, the films made during Nkrumah’s time were ordered to be burned. Hesse is the film’s unsung cinematic hero, along with his protégé, filmmaker and producer Anita Afonu. The documentary unveils a huge archive of surviving celluloid films from Africa’s liberation era in the 20th century, which were long thought to be destroyed but were quietly safeguarded by Hesse for more than 60 years. Bowers and Proudfoot previously worked together on the 2023 short The Last Repair Shop , which won the Documentary Short Film Oscar in 2024. The musician said he became involved with The Eyes of Ghana after Proudfoot sent him a sizzle reel of the footage he was working with. “I remember watching it in my car,” Bowers says. “After I finished watching it, I was filled with emotion just because of how much, as a Black man, my own history is lost. And it’s sad that at some point you have to give up. So, the idea that someone like Chris Hesse has preserved this history and a vision of people that look like me that I had never seen from that era made me feel incredibly moved.” The Eyes of Ghana was produced by Breakwater Studios ’ Proudfoot and Nana Adwoa Frimpong, Afonu, Bw

articles.content: A well-known British man has lost his bid for an injunction against ITN and The Guardian to prevent the media outlets from publishing allegations of sexual misconduct. In a High Court judgment, the star’s claim for an injunction was denied, but a temporary order preventing the man (known as PPT in court proceedings) from being named remains in place pending an appeal. Gavin Millar, who made the case for ITN and The Guardian , argued that the news organizations had a duty to publish information that was in the public interest. The two outlets are seeking to publish allegations of inappropriate and exploitative sexual activities with girls and young women based on the accounts of more than 30 sources, The Guardian reported. In a written submission to the court, PPT’s lawyers said: “It is important to understand that this drastic effect on the claimant is not from guilt of the wrongdoing alleged (which is denied) but because of shame arising from deep-rooted childhood trauma and the fear of ‘trial by media.'” The court heard that PPT had made two previous attempts to kill himself: In May, when ITN and The Guardian gave him an opportunity to respond to the allegations; and in July, when he absconded from a secure hospital. Paramount held a number of press screenings for the scandal-plagued A-lister’s big Hollywood comeback feature, Ebenezer , over the last few days and the first reactions are hitting social media. Ebenezer held its world premiere at the Whitby Hotel in New York City on Nov. 1. The film had its London premiere in Leicester Square on Monday night. Full critics reviews for the film drop on Nov. 12, but Paramount allowed people who had attended the various screenings to post brief reactions to the film on social media. Ebenezer hits theaters globally on Nov. 13. Related Stories Movies Alan Ritchson Taps Alex Jackson to Serve as President at Dancing Skeleton Production Company Movies Helene Hahn Loyd, Former Disney and DreamWorks Exec, Dies at 78 The latest adaptation of Charles Dickens’ classic 1843 novella A Christmas Carol , Ebenezer is a more black comedy take on the trials and tribulations of one Ebenezer Scrooge. Set in Victorian London, the film follows Scrooge (Depp), a miserly businessman who has a particular hatred for Christmas. Scrooge goes on a redemption journey after being visited by three spirits. The film has a stellar cast featuring the likes of Tramell Tillman , Ian McKellen , Rupert Grint , Andrea Riseborough , Sam Claflin , Daisy Ridley , Arthur Conti, Ellie Bamber and Henry Lloyd-Hughes. Ebenezer is directed by Ti West , the filmmaker behind A24’s highly regarded X trilogy as well as The Roost (2005), Trigger Man (2007), The House of the Devil (2009), The Innkeepers (2011) and In a Valley of Violence (2016). Nathaniel Halpern wrote the screenplay. There is a lot riding on Ebenezer for Depp. The film is the Oscar-nominated actor’s first mainstream Hollywood feature since the fallout from his divorce from Amber Heard and subsequent legal battles. articles.title: ‘Summer School, 2001,’ the First Czech-Vietnamese Feature, Is Coming to America via Cinemas, Amazon (Exclusive)
articles.summary: Two diaspora groups can hit Cinemark theaters from Dec. 11 for a limited run of the award-winning debut feature directed by Dužan Duong, courtesy of Reel Citrus, before two big studio tentpole releases hit.
articles.content: In 2025, Summer School, 2001 , the debut feature of writer-director Dužan Duong and dubbed the “first Czech-Vietnamese feature film,” made a splash at the Karlovy Vary International Film Festival and beyond. Now, it is coming to America, courtesy of Reel Citrus, an L.A.-based distributor of Asian and diaspora films. The company will open Summer School, 2001 in a limited U.S. theatrical release on Dec. 11 at Cinemark cinemas, hitting screens before Dune 3 and Avengers: Doomsday opens a week later. The film will then stream on Amazon from Dec. 18 before rolling out globally. Related Stories Movies Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama 'I Is Another' Sells Wide Ahead of AFM Business The Hollywood Reporter Launches Turkish Edition “At a time when immigration and belonging are front-page news in both the U.S. and Europe, the release brings two diasporas into the same theater,” said Reel Citrus. Summer School, 2001 follows 17-year-old Kien, who returns to his family’s market stall in Cheb, a small town on the Czech border, after spending 10 years in Vietnam. It becomes a chaotic summer, during which the family must try to become whole again. After its Karlovy Vary world premiere, the movie drew more than 20,000 moviegoers during its run in Czech cinemas. At the Czech Lion Awards, the Czech national film honors, Summer School, 2001 won the best screenplay award for Duong, Jan Smutný and Lukáš Kokeš, along with the best supporting actor honor for Dũng Nguyễn, the first Vietnamese actor to win a Czech Lion. The Czech Film Critics’ Awards named it the best screenplay and the Discovery of the Year. At Viet Film Fest, the largest U.S. festival for the Vietnamese diaspora, the film won the Bronze Drum (Trống Đồng) Award for the best feature film, the best actor honor for Tô Tiến Tài and the Audience Choice Award for best feature. articles.title: Ariana Grande on First Time Meeting Ben Stiller: “Directing Me in an Orgy Scene in ‘Zoolander 2’”
articles.summary: Grande and Stiller have since reunited in 'Focker-in-Law,' which releases Nov. 25.
articles.content: Ariana Grande won’t be forgetting the first time she met Ben Stiller anytime soon. During a recent episode of The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon , Grande, Stiller and Robert De Niro made a joint appearance to chat about their new film Focker-in-Law , which releases on Nov. 25. At one point, host Jimmy Fallon asked the Grammy-winning singer about the first time she met Stiller, to which she replied, “I met Ben in a very different way,” drawing laughter from the audience. In the 2016 action-comedy, directed by Stiller, Derek (Stiller) and Hansel (Owen Wilson) are lured into the fashion world again, in Rome, where they find themselves the target of a sinister conspiracy. articles.title: Jessica Lange on Bringing ‘Long Day’s Journey Into Night’ Back to the Big Screen, Returning to ‘American Horror Story’ and Retirement Rumors
articles.summary: The legendary stage and screen actress spoke with The Hollywood Reporter at the recent Virginia Film Festival, where she was honored with the fest's Visionary Award.
articles.content: “You age out of a lot of parts, that’s just the nature of things,” Jessica Lange , the legendary stage and screen actress, said during a recent recording of The Hollywood Reporter ’s Awards Chatter podcast at the Virginia Film Festival , where she was being honored with the fest’s Visionary Award . The 77-year-old, who also brought to the fest her latest film, a big-screen adaptation of Long Day’s Journey Into Night , was discussing the possibility of retirement and continued, “I wouldn’t mind ending on Mary Tyrone [the protagonist of Long Day’s Journey , a morphine addict in 1912 Connecticut], let me tell you. articles.title: Nicole Avant to Receive Visionary Producer Award at Bahamas International Film Festival (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The producer and former ambassador to the Bahamas will also be bestowed with the title of Honorary Patron of the Bahamas International Film Festival.
articles.content: Producer and former U.S. Ambassador to the Bahamas Nicole Avant will receive the Visionary Producer Award at this year’s Bahamas International Film Festival . It’s a full circle moment for Avant, who is also being honored with the title of honorary patron of BIFF, as the award-winning producer, best-selling author and philanthropist attended the 2009 edition of the festival while the ambassador to the Bahamas. Avant will be honored on the opening night gala of the festival, whose main part runs Dec. 10 to 14 in Nassau, after a three-day affair featuring a screenwriters residency and select film screenings in Harbour Island. The Visionary Producer Award recognizes Avant’s distinctive body of work as a producer who brings powerful and often untold stories to the screen. articles.summary: Jackson, a vet of Paramount, MRC and Chernin Entertainment, will certainly have plenty to do at the in-demand actor's production company which is shepherding projects at Amazon MGM Studios and Netflix.

articles.title: Claes Bang, Valerie Pachner Drama ‘I Is Another’ Sells Wide Ahead of AFM
articles.summary: The Felix Randau-directed historical film about Heinrich Himmler’s massage therapist premiered to strong reviews at Locarno.
articles.content: Beta Cinema has closed a raft of international sales for I Is Another , Felix Randau’s historical drama starring Claes Bang and Valerie Pachner, ahead of the American Film Market. ARP Selection acquired all rights for France, with further deals signed with Youplanet Pictures for Spain, Angel Films for Scandinavia, Big Tree Entertainment for India and Palace Films for Australia and New Zealand. Vertigo Media took Hungary, Beta Film acquired Bulgaria and Red Cape picked up Israel. The deals were unveiled Monday on the eve of AFM , following the film’s world premiere on Locarno’s Piazza Grande this summer. Related Stories Business The Hollywood Reporter Launches Turkish Edition Movies Jonathan Bailey and Bill Nighy to Star in Oliver Sacks Love Story 'Insomniac City' Based on true events, I Is Another stars Bang as Felix Kersten, massage therapist to SS leader Heinrich Himmler . Said to have helped secure the release of thousands of concentration camp prisoners, Kersten is traveling to Oslo in the hope of winning the Nobel Peace Prize. Aboard the night train, however, he faces an interview with Hedda (Pachner), a journalist convinced he is an impostor. Their encounter becomes a contest over memory, truth and the version of his life Kersten wants the world to believe. Port-au-Prince Pictures will release the film in Germany in early 2027. ARP Selection is introducing it to French audiences at the Augenblick Film Festival ahead of a nationwide theatrical release next year. Randau ( Iceman , Northern Star ) wrote and directed the film, which was produced by Ostlicht Filmproduktion in co-production with Veit Heiduschka’s Wega Film. The cast also includes Susanne Wuest, Timocin Ziegler and Martin Müller, with Sebastian Thaler serving as director of photography. Beta Cinema will hold an AFM screening on Nov. 11 at 9 a.m. at AMC Century City 3. The American Film Market runs Nov. 10-15.

articles.title: Jonathan Bailey and Bill Nighy to Star in Oliver Sacks Love Story ‘Insomniac City’
articles.summary: Dominic Cooke will direct the adaptation of Bill Hayes’ memoir, with Altitude launching worldwide sales at AFM.
articles.content: Jonathan Bailey and Bill Nighy are set to star in Insomniac City , director Dominic Cooke’s adaptation of writer and photographer Bill Hayes’ memoir about his romance with celebrated neurologist Oliver Sacks. The casting was unveiled Monday on the eve of the American Film Market in Los Angeles, where Altitude will introduce the project to international buyers. Bailey ( Bridgerton ) will play Hayes opposite Nighy ( About Time ) as Sacks. Adapted from Hayes’ 2017 memoir, the film follows his move from San Francisco to New York in the aftermath of a devastating loss. As he rebuilds his life, Hayes unexpectedly falls in love with both his adopted city and Sacks, beginning a relationship that transformed both men’s lives during the neurologist’s final years. Related Stories Movies 'KPop Demon Hunters' Directors Board Animated Short 'Living With a Visionary' as Exec Producers (Exclusive) Oscars 2027: Int'l Films in Focus 'Shame and Money' Director Explains Why His Int'l Oscar Hopeful About Dignity Feels So Physical Sacks’ work famously includes The Man Who Mistook His Wife for a Hat and Awakenings , the latter adapted into the Oscar-nominated film starring Robin Williams and Robert De Niro. Cooke, whose directing credits include The Courier and On Chesil Beach , co-wrote the screenplay with Hayes. “ Insomniac City is a rare story that feels both profoundly intimate and epic in scope,” Cooke said in a statement. “It is also a love letter to New York City itself, a place of endless possibility, reinvention and connection.” Troy Lum and Andrew Mason are producing for their U.K.-Australian banner Brouhaha Entertainment alongside Bailey, Mike Goodridge and Gabrielle Tana. Altitude’s Will Clarke, Andy Mayson and Mike Runagall will executive produce.

articles.content: KPop Demon Hunters directors and Oscar winners Maggie Kang and Chris Appelhans have boarded the award-winning animated short film Living With a Visionary as executive producers. Narrated by James Cromwell, the documentary, written, directed and animated by Stephen P. Neary, is a reflection on a poet’s 50-year marriage to an art curator grappling with Parkinson’s. The news comes before The New York Times Op-Docs will premiere the short this week. Living With a Visionary recently won the grand jury award for animation at AFI Fest after earlier this year being honored with the short film jury award for animation at the Sundance Film Festival. The creator drew them over the course of three years at nights and on weekends while working full-time as a story artist and teaching classes at the California Institute of the Arts. articles.title: James Gunn “Incredibly Relieved” to Leave DC Studios: Job Was “Trying, to Say the Least”
articles.summary: The DC Studios co-chief admits that the executive role wasn't quite right for him and looks forward to returning to filmmaking full time.
articles.content: That’s according to Gunn, who posted a farewell message on Instagram in the wake of the surprising news that he and Peter Safran were exiting the top studio roles and Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham was taking over. articles.title: Ridley Scott Will Miss Academy’s Governors Awards, Accept Honorary Oscar Remotely (Exclusive)
articles.summary: The 88-year-old, who is based in London, underwent a minor medical procedure last week and has been advised not to fly while he is still healing, sources tell The Hollywood Reporter.
articles.content: The legendary filmmaker Ridley Scott , who was tapped to receive an honorary Oscar at the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences’ 17th annual Governors Awards on Sunday night, will not be able to attend the ceremony in Hollywood to accept the honor in-person, The Hollywood Reporter can exclusively report. Scott, who is based in London and will turn 89 on Nov. 30, underwent a minor medical procedure last week and has been advised not to fly while he is still healing, sources tell THR . However, Scott’s entire family — his wife, children and grandchildren — will be making the trip to L.A. for this celebration. Skydance, which now oversees the division thanks to its acquisition of Warner Bros. articles.summary: Danish star Trine Dyrholm, a former cult member and one of the three directors of the hybrid doc, debuting at Tallinn, explain how they approached reenactments and more in their cinematic experiment.
articles.content: Father’s House ( Faderhuset ) not only charted an unusual path to explore mechanisms of control in a hybrid documentary about the Danish Christian sect Faderhuset, or “Father’s House.” It also aims to make you think about manipulation in a broader sense that goes well beyond the experience of how this specific cult evolved in the 1990s into a tightly controlled community held together by faith, manipulation and abuse. The film features reenactments, with former members helping the actors bring to life their real-life experiences, exchanges between them and former cult insiders sharing their insights on their past. articles.title: BBC Studios Names Sreya Biswas New Head of Its Natural History Unit
articles.summary: Reporting to Kate Ward, managing director, unscripted at BBC Studios, she will work alongside creative directors Mike Gunton and Jonny Keeling.
articles.content: BBC Studios has named Sreya Biswas the new head of its Natural History Unit (NHU). She takes over from Jonny Keeling, who is moving into a new role from early 2027, as previously unveiled. Reporting to Kate Ward , managing director, unscripted at BBC Studios , Biswas will work alongside creative directors Keeling and Mike Gunton, overseeing the unit’s teams based in Bristol. “Biswas will lead the editorial, commercial and strategic direction for the NHU as it sets an ambitious growth strategy for the future,” the company said. Biswas joined BBC Studios in the summer 2025 as the NHU’s Director of programs, where she oversaw a number of commissioned titles and the development of a portfolio of new content for multiple global clients across platforms, including the first BBC visualized nature podcast Naturewatch, feature documentary Matriarch , and Blue Planet III . Previously, she was served as head of commissioning for Natural History at the BBC, where she oversaw some of the landmark TV series, including Planet Earth III, Asia, Kingdom and Blue Planet III , as well as commissioning a broad range of natural history content, including Big Cats 24/7, Hamza’s Hidden Wild Isles, Spy in the Troop and A n Hour on Earth . articles.content: A few images speak much louder than many words in Moisés Kaufman and Amanda Gronich’s play about the Holocaust So much for the power of live theater. It happens whenever a director decides to unspool a film or place blown-up photographs among living-breathing actors on stage. When an audience is given the choice to follow a human or a projection, the eye goes to the projection. Moisés Kaufman and Amanda Gronich’s play “Here There Are Blueberries” opened Monday at the Barrymore Theater after engagements Off Broadway and elsewhere. The photographs projected on stage, taken at Auschwitz and its environs during World War II, are nothing short of unforgettable. The actors on stage are something less. Late in “Here There Are Blueberries,” we see the more familiar photos. These are the images of Jews arriving by train at Auschwitz, surrounded by the Nazi guards and their dogs. They are shocking. But equally disturbing for very different reasons are the happy photographs displayed earlier in the play. These photographs – 116 of them — include no images of Jewish prisoners, but rather the commandants and the employees of Auschwitz. And these Nazis are having a great time. The men in uniform sing, picnic, enjoy a beer at the end of a long hard day at the concentration camp. Other photos show female telephone operators from Auschwitz being treated to a dessert of blueberries at Solahutte, a lodge retreat snuggled among the pine trees nearby. From another album, photographs show children enjoying themselves in a backyard pool. Only on closer inspection do we notice a guard tower at Auschwitz just over the ivy-covered wall. These Nazis-having-a-good-time photos recall the Oscar-winning film “The Zone of Interest,” but are more disturbing because the people in the photographs are not actors. articles.content: From “Project Hail Mary” to “La Bola Negra” and “You Can See Everything,” this awards season is dominated by director duos. Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo , better known as Los Javis, are seen as locks for “La Bola Negra,” the Netflix-backed gay historical epic, while longtime collaborators Phil Lord and Chris Miller are also firmly in the Oscar conversation for their work on “Project Hail Mary.” Then there’s Emmy nominee Nathan Fielder teaming up with documentary-world wunderkind Lance Oppenheim on “You Can See Everything,” a less conventional contender, but one that could muscle itself into the race thanks to its box office success. Plus “Clarissa” from brothers Arie and Chuko Esiri, and “Mouse” from director couple Kelly O’Sullivan and Alex Thompson, which picked up a Gotham Best Feature nom. That’s six different films in this year’s awards conversation, suggesting director duos are becoming more common in filmmaking overall. articles.summary: ToruńCAMERIMAGE promised to devote its 2026 edition to "the hopes and threats of AI." The discussions are more than living up to that.
articles.content: During the opening ceremony of the 34th Toruń CAMERIMAGE International Film Festival on Saturday, November 7, audience members saw a human replaced by a machine right in front of their eyes. The festival’s founder and artistic director Marek Żydowicz was invited to the stage, only for a robot to walk out in his place and begin addressing the audience and thanking sponsors. Żydowicz took the stage a few moments later and joked that none of us are immune to the threat of AI and robots coming for our jobs. articles.title: ‘You Can See Everything’ Sweeps Critics Choice Documentary Awards
articles.summary: The Critics Choice Association gave the Nathan Fielder-Lance Oppenheim documentary five awards, including the top prize.
articles.content: “You Can See Everything,” Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim ‘s phenomenally successful documentary about disgraced Theranos founder Elizabeth Holmes, swept the Critics Choice Association ‘s documentary awards tonight, winning each of its five categories — including Best Documentary Feature. Ava DuVernay’s “14th,” which headed into the night with the most nominations (six), went home empty-handed. In addition to the top prize, “You Can See Everything” won Best Director (Fielder and Oppenheimer), Best Cinematography (David Bolen), Best Editing (Adam Locke-Norton), and Best Music Score (Ari Balouzian). Whether or not this is a harbinger of the film ‘s Oscar chances is anybody’s guess. A24 is aggressively campaigning for “You Can See Everything” to score both Best Documentary and Best Picture nominations. If the film receives the latter, it would be the first documentary ever to do so. The CCA sweep certainly doesn’t hurt its prospects, but it’s not necessarily a predictor either — in the last 10 years, the CCA and Academy have only agreed on the best documentary twice (with “O.J.: Made in America” and “Summer of Soul”). articles.title: Box Office: ‘Godzilla Minus Zero’ Thunders with $31.6 Million, Scoring the Biggest Debut Ever for a Live-Action, Foreign Language Film
articles.summary: "Godzilla Minus Zero" continues a streak of unlikely blockbusters and shows moviegoers don't care about subtitles.
articles.content: The year of unlikely box office smashes continues as “ Godzilla Minus Zero ” opened to a thunderous $31.6 million, shattering records to become the biggest North American debut for a live-action foreign language film in history. It easily toppled the previous benchmark established in 2002 by the wuxia epic “Hero,” which kicked off with $17.8 million. Globally, “Godzilla Minus Zero’s” haul stands at $63 million. And it comes on the heels of a string of films that have defied conventional wisdom to resonate with moviegoers. Yes, the box office is still dominated by sequels and comic book movies like “Toy Story 5” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” but there’s been a lot more variety. Audiences have turned out in force for an original sci-fi adventure (“Project Hail Mary,” $684.6 million worldwide); a pair of low-budget horror films from 20-something auteurs with YouTube pedigree (“Obsession,” $524.3 million worldwide; “Backrooms,” $400.6 million worldwide); an adaptation of a Greek epic we were all forced to read in school (“The Odyssey,” $1.8 billion worldwide), and a three-hour documentary about a Silicon Valley cheat (“You Can See Everything,” $73.7 million and counting). Clearly, people are looking for something different.
